navratri: Sharad Navratri 2026 starts on Sunday 11 October with Ghatasthapana and runs nine nights to Monday 19 October. Vijayadashami (Dussehra) is on Tuesday 20 October 2026.
What are the nine Navratri colours for 2026?
Day 1 to Day 9: Orange, White, Red, Royal Blue, Yellow, Green, Grey, Purple and Peacock Green. Colour conventions can differ slightly by region.
Where can I find garba and dandiya events in Pune?

Pune Ganpati LIVE lists community-submitted garba and dandiya events with venue, date, time and booking link. Organisers can submit an event for free by email. Always confirm timings and entry rules with the organiser.
Where can I rent a garba outfit or chaniya choli in Pune?

BlinkWear.in is a fashion rental marketplace with a hub in Pune. It offers festive lehengas and Navratri looks with rentals from Rs 499 per day, doorstep delivery and pickup. Check current availability on the BlinkWear website.
Which Devi temples can I visit in Pune during Navratri?

Well-known options include Chaturshringi Mata Mandir on Senapati Bapat Road and the Tambdi Jogeshwari temple in the old city. Expect long queues on weekends and on Ashtami; check the temple trust for darshan timings.
diwali: Diwali (Lakshmi Puja) is on Sunday 8 November 2026. Dhanteras is on 6 November, Govardhan Puja on 10 November and Bhai Dooj on 11 November. Puja muhurat varies by panchang.
Where to shop for Diwali in Pune?

Laxmi Road, Tulshibaug and the Peth-area markets are traditional festive shopping areas for clothes, lamps, decor and puja items. Evenings are crowded with traffic diversions, so the metro is the easiest way into the old city.
Where can I rent festive outfits for Diwali parties in Pune?
BlinkWear.in rents designer lehengas, ethnic wear and dresses with doorstep delivery and pickup, with rentals from Rs 499 per day. Check availability for your date on the BlinkWear website.
events: Which festivals are coming up in Pune in October and November 2026?
Sharad Navratri (11-19 October), Dussehra (20 October), Dhanteras (6 November), Diwali (8 November), Govardhan Puja (10 November) and Bhai Dooj (11 November).
